title: Params of Chaos
subtitle: Every `&` and `%` has a job.
description: Parse a URL query string correctly: pairs split on `&`, values on the first `=`, `+` means space, and percent escapes decode to UTF-8.
prompt: Given a query string (no leading `?`), split it into `key=value` pairs and decode both sides. Rules: pairs are separated by `&`; a pair may have no `=` (value is empty); `+` decodes to a space; `%XX` sequences decode as UTF-8.
instructions: Read one query string from input.
Print each decoded pair as `key=value` on its own line, in order.
constraints: The input contains only valid pairs and well-formed escapes.

examples.title: Example 1
examples.explanation: The `+` in the value decodes to a space.

examples.title: Example 2
examples.explanation: Only the FIRST `=` splits key from value; the rest is data.

hints: Values may legitimately contain `=` — how would `indexOf` help?

solution.summary: Split on `&`, then split each pair on its first `=` only. Decode `+` → space before percent-decoding, on both sides.
approach: `split("&")` is safe here because raw `&` cannot appear inside a properly encoded pair.
Use `indexOf("=")` — never `split("=")` — so values may contain `=`.
Replace `+` with a space, then apply `decodeURIComponent`.

code.label: Reference solution

commonMistakes: Decoding before splitting on `&` — an encoded `%26` would be corrupted.

learningObjectives: Parse query strings per the URL spec
